record.paper_title: A Survey on LoRa Networking: Research Problems, Current Solutions and Open Issues
record.context_brief: Dynamic retransmission policies for constrained LoRa hardware
record.original_question: How can LoRa networks set retransmission timers dynamically, across different deployment scenarios, so that end-devices do not retransmit messages that were already received correctly but whose acknowledgments were delayed or corrupted? A satisfactory policy should account for experimentally identified retransmission triggers, work on constrained LoRa hardware, and remain modular rather than depending necessarily on computationally expensive combinations of retransmission, channel coding, and compression.

evidence.quote: The third issue is the limited interval for retransmission. Due to the above said factors, ACKs may take more time to reach an end-device which will increase the retransmission probability even for a successfully delivered message.

Although the performance has been proved theoretically, its implementation with the required computational resource on real-time testbeds will be more helpful to understand the practical efﬁciency for real-world deployments.

Static retransmission policy degrades the network performance when the time taken by an ACK to reach the end node is larger than the retransmission time. This explains the need for dynamic retransmission policies.

A joint retransmission policy with channel coding and compression is theoretically studied, but the implementation of such computationally expensive techniques on constrained LoRa hardware must be considered in future. Besides, it has to be noted that a modular retransmission policy without any dependencies on other techniques is inevitable.

None of the techniques has addressed this problem of varying retransmission timers dynamically. The factors triggering retransmission, even in the case of correct reception, must be extensively studied through experiments for various scenarios and a dynamic policy must be devised to improve the performance of LoRa.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a low-power wide-area network in which end-devices transmit uplink messages to a gateway over a lossy wireless channel and expect downlink acknowledgments (ACKs) within a retransmission timer T. If an ACK is not received before T expires, the device retransmits the message; this wastes energy and channel time when the original message was in fact received correctly but its ACK was delayed beyond T or corrupted in transit. Each end-device has tight constraints on memory, computation, and energy, and the channel exhibits highly variable delay distributions across different deployment scenarios (e.g., urban, rural, indoor, mobile).

Design a dynamic retransmission-timer policy T = T(state) — where 'state' may include locally observable quantities such as past ACK round-trip times, recent loss/duplicate-ACK events, spreading factor, duty-cycle constraints, and coarse load indicators — with the following requirements:

1. Trigger awareness: the policy must explicitly mitigate retransmissions whose triggering cause is a delayed or corrupted ACK rather than a lost uplink message, using empirically identifiable retransmission triggers.
2. Hardware feasibility: the policy must be implementable on resource-constrained end-device hardware (limited RAM, no floating-point unit, limited energy budget) and produce decisions in real time.
3. Modularity: the policy must function as a stand-alone retransmission mechanism, without requiring joint operation with channel coding or payload compression.
4. Cross-scenario robustness: the policy must achieve, across heterogeneous deployment scenarios, a provable or empirically demonstrated improvement over any static choice of T in terms of expected number of redundant retransmissions per successfully delivered message, while keeping the message delivery probability and end-to-end latency at least as good as a tuned static baseline.

Provide such a policy together with an analysis (or testbed-validated evaluation) establishing properties (1)–(4).
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published dynamic LoRa retransmission-timer policy that simultaneously satisfies all four requirements (empirically grounded trigger awareness, constrained-hardware implementation, modularity independent of joint channel coding/compression, and cross-scenario robustness). Subsequent literature on LoRaWAN ADR and reliability typically addresses adaptive data rate, ACK-less reliability, or joint coding schemes rather than a stand-alone dynamic retransmission timer of the form requested. The problem therefore appears to remain open.
